key_insight: WorldRuler explores interactive world models that follow configurable, user-defined rules rather than only real-world behavior. The central challenge is keeping those rules consistent over time and making their effects visible in generated worlds.
problem_solved: Customizable gameplay requires models to preserve rule definitions, dependencies, and world states across saving and loading, while translating rules into appropriate visual outcomes. The provided abstract is truncated, so specific solutions and results cannot be verified.
method: Frame interactive world modeling around configurable rules that determine how player actions change a world.
Address Rule-State Persistence: maintaining rules, their dependencies, and world state across save/load cycles.
Address Rule-to-Visual Realization: translating user-defined rules into visible world changes. Implementation details are not available in the excerpt.
impact: Rule-configurable world models could enable more customizable games and interactive simulations. For practitioners, the paper highlights persistent state management and rule-consistent visual generation as essential design challenges.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: user-defined rules + player action + current state → updated visual world.

Two challenge icons: a database for persistence and an image frame for visual realization.
paper_title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
paper_authors: Mingliang Zhai, Chuanhao Li, Jiaming Tan, Zhen Li, Yuwei Wu
